questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Dangerous intersections.
Slow-moving vehicles.
Yield signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicles.
questions.explanation: A reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it moves slowly. You may see it on farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons. It looks like a solid orange triangle during the day and a hollow red triangle at night.

questions.question: You have a green light, but traffic is blocking the intersection ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
Follow other vehicles and enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if traffic is blocking it, even if your light is green. If you enter and the light turns red, you will block other traffic and may get a ticket.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
One-way.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when should you move back to the right lane?

options.text: When you are one vehicle length ahead of the other vehicle.
When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only move back to your lane when you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed. When both headlights appear in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to your lane.

questions.question: When planning to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the other driver will keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you space or let you pass, even if you signal. Make sure the space is clear before you move.

questions.question: On an interstate, traffic is merging from on-ramps on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Keep your speed and position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to the left.
questions.explanation: When you see an on-ramp ahead, move to the left lane when safe. This gives vehicles entering the highway space to merge.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase the space between you and the vehicle ahead when it is dark. Use your headlights properly and avoid looking at oncoming headlights to prevent being blinded.

questions.question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, use:

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect back at you in these conditions and create glare that makes it hard to see.

questions.question: The best way to avoid a dangerous situation while driving is to:

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always keep your eyes focused ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay aware of everything around you—front, sides, and rear. This helps you spot problems early and change your speed or position if needed.

questions.question: You and another driver reach a four-way stop at the same time. The other driver is on your left. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left has the right-of-way.
You have the right-of-way.
Whoever is signaling to turn has the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as other traffic (as long as they follow the speed limit). Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot hit each other. Most crashes happen when some vehicles drive faster or slower than others.

questions.question: When parallel parking facing downhill, what should you do with your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the side of the road.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or edge of the road. When parking uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross it to pass. A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass, but only if it is safe.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must help keep the road safe. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed for:

options.text: Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
The truck driver to stop the vehicle.
Other drivers when they want to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck driver to stop the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Trucks are larger and need more time to stop than cars. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn:

options.text: They may use the left lane.
They may cut through all lanes.
They may wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride with traffic on the road. It is normal to see a bicyclist using the left lane when turning.

questions.question: You are crossing an intersection and an emergency vehicle is approaching with its siren and flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or siren, finish crossing the intersection. Then drive to the right and stop. You must give the right-of-way to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using lights or sirens.

questions.question: It is dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely because:

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.
A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.
They brake more slowly than motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop quickly. Following too closely puts both you and the motorcyclist in danger. You need enough space and time to stop if the motorcyclist makes a sudden move.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
School crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to possible hazards. This sign warns drivers that pedestrians may cross the road.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.
Turn on your high beam headlights to better see the vehicles ahead of you.
Keep the instrument panel lights bright to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.
questions.explanation: Drive slower at night than during the day because you cannot see as far ahead. Make sure you can stop within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: You should leave extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the motorcycle brakes or the rider falls off. Motorcycles are also hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A downward-pointing triangle is always a yield sign. You must slow down or stop when you see a yield sign.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Does not increase the chance of a crash.
Helps you react faster to danger.
Often makes you make risky driving choices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often makes you make risky driving choices.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast is a major cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to poor driving decisions.

questions.question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic light means you:

options.text: May turn in that direction after slowing and checking traffic.
Cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
May turn in that direction after a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: How often should you check your speedometer?

options.text: Once every ten minutes
Twice a minute
Once a minute

questions.correctAnswerText: Once a minute
questions.explanation: Look at your speedometer about once every minute to make sure you are driving at a safe and legal speed. Make this a habit.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Move to another lane while in an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane while in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Before changing lanes, always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Watch for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a downhill ramp that curves. You should:

options.text: Slow down to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow down to the posted freeway speed limit.
Wait until you are in the curve to start braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You may not see hazards ahead, and braking in a curve can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow-moving vehicle.
Road construction or maintenance area.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.
Wait four seconds before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means go. Turn in the direction the arrow points after yielding to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: Your vehicle's wheels have gone off the edge of the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly left to get back onto the pavement.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently apply the brakes.
Brake hard and turn the front wheels sharply to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes. Slow down, check traffic, and find a safe place to return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel suddenly, as this can cause you to lose control or enter other lanes.
